identity.title: RAIN-Merging: A Gradient-Free Method to Enhance Instruction Following in Large Reasoning Models with Preserved Thinking Format

problem.claim: The paper asks whether integrating an instruction-tuned model into a large reasoning model can improve adherence to output formats, constraints, and requirements.

gap.claim: Naïve parameter merging is described as fragile because it overlooks the mismatch between explicit thinking/response segments in reasoning models and answers-only outputs in instruction-tuned models.

contributions.claim: RAIN-Merging is a gradient-free, reasoning-aware merging method designed to integrate instruction following while preserving thinking format and reasoning performance.
The method projects instruction-model task vectors into a null space defined by forward features at thinking special tokens, then applies module-specific scaling derived from instruction attention.
The authors report that task-vector principal subspaces are nearly orthogonal across key modules, motivating lightweight merging with minimal interference.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present RAIN-Merging as a reasoning-aware, instruction-attention-guided null-space projection approach for gradient-free model merging that preserves the reasoning model’s thinking format.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report substantial improvement in instruction adherence across four instruction-following benchmarks while maintaining reasoning quality across nine reasoning and general-capability benchmarks.
The authors report consistent gains across model scales and architectures, with improved performance in agent settings.

narrative_sequence.summary: Large reasoning models are strong at long-chain reasoning but often fail format and constraint-following requirements.
The paper investigates whether an instruction-tuned model can close this instruction-following gap when integrated into a reasoning model.
Parameter-space analysis suggests low interference from near-orthogonal task-vector subspaces, but naïve merging fails to account for thinking-format mismatch.
RAIN-Merging uses null-space projection and instruction-attention-guided scaling; the authors report better instruction adherence while preserving reasoning quality across benchmarks and settings.

source_observation.claim: The abstract explicitly identifies an output-format mismatch as a failure mode of naïve merging and makes preservation of thinking tokens a design target.

lessons.interpretation: When combining models with different output protocols, compatibility constraints may need to be part of the merge objective rather than treated as a downstream formatting issue.
lessons.application: Define representation- or token-level invariants for each model’s output protocol, then constrain parameter updates against those invariants during integration.
lessons.exception: This move may be unsuitable when the models share the same output protocol or when preserving the original protocol is not a goal.

unknowns: The abstract gives no numerical results, baseline definitions, statistical analyses, or benchmark-specific conditions.
It does not specify the calibration-set sizes, projection details, scaling formula, or which model scales and architectures were evaluated.
The claimed agent-setting improvement and near-orthogonality are not quantified in the supplied units.
